Enqueue: `MailJob.perform_async(1)` or via Active Job `MailJob.perform_later(@user.id)`. Set options: `sidekiq_options queue: :mailers, retry: 5`. Keep perform small and focused (one job, one task); make it idempotent (safe to retry). Logging: `Sidekiq::Logging.logger`. Don't do huge work in one job — split it (one job per item, or batch). Avoid long-running jobs (they hold a thread); set a timeout. Test the job directly (perform) and via the queue.

sections.content:
```ruby
# A Sidekiq worker: include Sidekiq::Job + def perform
class MailJob
  include Sidekiq::Job                  # marks it as a job (was Sidekiq::Worker)
  sidekiq_options queue: :mailers, retry: 5

  def perform(user_id)                  # args are JSON-serialized -> pass IDs
    user = User.find(user_id)
    Mailer.welcome(user).deliver_now
  end
end

# Enqueue (returns immediately):
MailJob.perform_async(1)                # direct Sidekiq
# or via Active Job:
MailJob.perform_later(1)
MailJob.set(wait: 5.minutes).perform_later(1)

# Args must be JSON-serializable (pass IDs, not objects):
#   BAD:  MailJob.perform_async(@user)      # whole object (won't survive JSON)
#   GOOD: MailJob.perform_async(@user.id)   # then User.find in perform
#   symbols -> strings; complex objects -> don't survive; use IDs/hashes of primitives

# Keep perform SMALL and FOCUSED (one job, one task); make IDEMPOTENT.
class PdfJob
  include Sidekiq::Job
  def perform(report_id)
    r = Report.find(report_id)
    return if r.pdf_generated?      # IDEMPOTENT: don't regenerate
    r.generate_pdf
  end
end

# Split big work (one job per item), avoid long-running jobs (hold a thread):
#   ids.each { |id| ProcessItemJob.perform_async(id) }   # many small jobs

# Logging: Sidekiq::Logging.logger.info("done #{user_id}")
# Test the job DIRECTLY (MailJob.new.perform(1)) and via the queue.
```

A worker is a class with `perform` that does the work.

Minimal: `class MailJob; include Sidekiq::Job; def perform(user_id); User.find(user_id).send_mail; end; end`.

`include Sidekiq::Job` (formerly Sidekiq::Worker) marks it as a job. `perform` takes simple args (IDs, strings, numbers, arrays/hashes of those) — they're JSON-serialized to Redis, so pass IDs not objects. Enqueue: `MailJob.perform_async(1)` or via Active Job `MailJob.perform_later(@user.id)`. Set options: `sidekiq_options queue: :mailers, retry: 5`. Keep perform small and focused (one job, one task); make it idempotent (safe to retry). Logging: `Sidekiq::Logging.logger`. Don't do huge work in one job — split it (one job per item, or batch). Avoid long-running jobs (they hold a thread); set a timeout. Test the job directly (perform) and via the queue.

sections.title: Sidekiq worker
sections.content:
```ruby
# A Sidekiq worker: include Sidekiq::Job + def perform
class MailJob
  include Sidekiq::Job                  # marks it as a job (was Sidekiq::Worker)
  sidekiq_options queue: :mailers, retry: 5

  def perform(user_id)                  # args are JSON-serialized -> pass IDs
    user = User.find(user_id)
    Mailer.welcome(user).deliver_now
  end
end

# Enqueue (returns immediately):
MailJob.perform_async(1)                # direct Sidekiq
# or via Active Job:
MailJob.perform_later(1)
MailJob.set(wait: 5.minutes).perform_later(1)

# Args must be JSON-serializable (pass IDs, not objects):
#   BAD:  MailJob.perform_async(@user)      # whole object (won't survive JSON)
#   GOOD: MailJob.perform_async(@user.id)   # then User.find in perform
#   symbols -> strings; complex objects -> don't survive; use IDs/hashes of primitives

# Keep perform SMALL and FOCUSED (one job, one task); make IDEMPOTENT.
class PdfJob
  include Sidekiq::Job
  def perform(report_id)
    r = Report.find(report_id)
    return if r.pdf_generated?      # IDEMPOTENT: don't regenerate
    r.generate_pdf
  end
end

# Split big work (one job per item), avoid long-running jobs (hold a thread):
#   ids.each { |id| ProcessItemJob.perform_async(id) }   # many small jobs

# Logging: Sidekiq::Logging.logger.info("done #{user_id}")
# Test the job DIRECTLY (MailJob.new.perform(1)) and via the queue.
```
